_comment: Per-tenant opt-in config for enforce-journal-tags.py. Copy to <trusted home>/.config/journal/journal-tags.json, where <trusted home> is the passwd/token home the OS resolves, never $HOME; set $JOURNAL_CONFIG_DIR to an absolute directory to place it elsewhere. With no config (or enabled != true) the hook no-ops, so a tenant who keeps no Daily Notes is never affected. The hook DENIES a Write/Edit/MultiEdit that ADDS an entry (a bold lead-in at column 0 followed by prose) to a Daily Note without a leading category tag, e.g. `[decision] **Retired the charter model.** Sam's call.` It reconstructs the before-document (from disk) and the after-document (the tool call applied) and denies only on an untagged entry line the write introduces, so overwriting or appending to a note full of legacy untagged entries is never blocked. EDITING an existing untagged entry does ask you to tag that one entry (its line changed); the entries you are not touching are never flagged. Bold-only header lines, fenced code blocks, HTML comments, <pre> blocks, any line containing a pipe, and column-0 bold sub-points inside an entry are not entries. tags is the allowed set (default: decision, fix, architecture, ops). daily_notes_dirs is the directory NAME set, matched as a path segment (default: Daily Notes); it is deliberately NOT a regex, because a user-supplied regex is a ReDoS foot-gun that can hang the hook past its timeout and stall every write. Disable entirely by naming enforce-journal-tags in $JOURNAL_DISABLED (the legacy $HARNESS_MANAGEMENT_DISABLED, under which this hook shipped in the monolith as enforce-daily-note-tags, disables it under EITHER name).
